explanation.concept: The four ways to interact with AWS
explanation.correct: The AWS Management Console is the browser-based UI for creating and managing resources. The other three access methods are the CLI, the SDKs, and the underlying API — all of them programmatic rather than web-based.

distractors.A: The CLI is a command-line tool you install and run in a terminal, not a web interface.
distractors.B: The API is the HTTPS interface everything else calls underneath; it has no UI of its own.
distractors.C: SDKs are language-specific libraries (Python, Java, JavaScript) for calling AWS from your own code.

explanation.concept: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
explanation.correct: Horizontal scaling means adding more instances of the same size — scaling out. It is the cloud-native approach because it has no upper bound and tolerates the loss of any single instance.

distractors.A: Replacing one instance with a bigger one is vertical scaling — scaling up.
distractors.B: Increasing the capacity of a single instance is vertical scaling.
distractors.C: Adding RAM to one instance is vertical scaling, and it requires a stop and restart.

explanation.concept: CloudTrail answers 'who did it'; CloudWatch answers 'how is it performing'
explanation.correct: AWS CloudTrail records every API call made in the account — who made it, from which IP, and when. Terminating an EC2 instance is an API call, so CloudTrail is where you find the responsible identity.

distractors.A: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; it does not log user actions.
distractors.C: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations on cost, performance, security and limits — not an audit trail.
distractors.D: The EC2 Instance Usage Report covers usage and cost data, not the identity behind an action.

explanation.concept: Reliability = recovering from failure and scaling to meet demand
explanation.correct: Reliability is the ability of a workload to perform correctly and consistently, which means both recovering quickly from failures (E) and acquiring resources automatically as demand changes (B).

distractors.A: Least privilege is a security principle, not a reliability one.
distractors.C: False — most AWS services are Region-scoped. Only a handful (IAM, Route 53, CloudFront) are global.
distractors.D: Service credits exist in the SLA, but compensation is a commercial remedy, not a reliability mechanism.

explanation.concept: The responsibility line moves with the service model
explanation.correct: The split depends on the service. With EC2 (IaaS) you patch the guest OS; with S3 or Lambda the provider handles far more. AWS is always responsible for security *of* the cloud, the customer for security *in* the cloud.

distractors.B: With IaaS the customer carries most of the security burden — OS, network config, and data.
distractors.C: Guest OS patching on EC2 is the customer's responsibility, never AWS's.
distractors.D: For managed services AWS handles the underlying infrastructure and platform patching.

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing shares Reserved Instance benefit across the whole organization
explanation.correct: Under consolidated billing, unused Reserved Instance capacity is shared across all accounts in the organization, so any account running a matching instance can receive the discounted hourly rate.

distractors.A: The benefit is not restricted to the management account — that is the point of sharing.
distractors.C: A Reserved Instance is a billing construct. It delivers identical performance to On-Demand.
distractors.D: Consolidated billing gives real savings through volume tiering and RI sharing, not just a single invoice.

explanation.concept: Availability tiers: AZ < Region
explanation.correct: Multiple Availability Zones protect against a data-centre failure; multiple Regions additionally protect against an entire Region becoming unavailable. Combining both gives the highest level of availability.

distractors.A: Edge locations cache content for CloudFront — they do not run your application.
distractors.B: Subnets live inside a single AZ, so adding subnets adds no availability beyond the AZs themselves.
distractors.D: Multiple VPCs in one Region share the same Regional failure domain.

explanation.concept: Snowball: physical device for bulk data transfer, with compute on board
explanation.correct: Snowball is a ruggedised physical appliance for securely moving large data sets into and out of AWS (E), and Snowball Edge variants include on-board compute so you can process data locally before shipping (A).

distractors.C: Hybrid storage between on-premises and AWS is AWS Storage Gateway.
distractors.D: Exabyte-scale transfer is Snowmobile, the shipping-container service — Snowball is petabyte-scale.

explanation.concept: Concierge is the Enterprise-plan billing specialist
explanation.correct: The AWS Support Concierge is a billing and account expert included with Enterprise Support, dedicated to non-technical billing and account inquiries.

distractors.A: The AWS Health Dashboard reports service health and events affecting your resources.
distractors.C: AWS Customer Service handles billing questions for all plans, but the Enterprise-specific, faster route is Concierge.
distractors.D: There is no AWS service called Operations Support.

explanation.concept: Latency is driven by physical distance — move the workload closer
explanation.correct: Deploying EC2 instances in a US Region places compute physically near the US users, which is the direct and low-cost way to cut latency.

distractors.A: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-centre service and has nothing to do with routing policies.
distractors.B: A domain name does not change where the servers are, so latency is unchanged.
distractors.C: Building a data centre is the most expensive option and contradicts the cost constraint.

explanation.concept: IAM groups attach permissions to a collection of users
explanation.correct: An IAM user group is a collection of IAM users that share an attached permission set — exactly the mechanism for organising employees into teams and granting each team its permissions.

distractors.A: Roles are assumed temporarily by users, applications or services; they are not a way to organise people into teams.
distractors.B: IAM users are individual identities — that is what you are trying to group.
distractors.D: AWS Organizations groups *accounts*, not users within an account.

explanation.concept: DMS migrates databases while the source stays online
explanation.correct: AWS Database Migration Service keeps the source database fully operational during migration and supports continuous replication, so applications keep running throughout the move.

distractors.A: OpsWorks is managed Chef/Puppet configuration management.
distractors.C: Server Migration Service migrates whole virtual machines, not databases specifically.
distractors.D: Application Discovery Service inventories your on-premises estate to plan a migration; it does not perform one.

explanation.concept: Elasticity: match supply to demand automatically
explanation.correct: Implementing elasticity means acquiring resources when demand rises and releasing them when it falls, so you stop paying for idle capacity.

distractors.A: Security in every layer is a separate design principle about defence in depth.
distractors.B: Parallelising tasks is about throughput and concurrency, not cost-driven capacity changes.
distractors.D: AWS recommends the opposite of monolithic architecture — decoupled, loosely joined components.

explanation.concept: Cloud benefits: agility, and inheriting AWS's security controls
explanation.correct: Provisioning in minutes rather than weeks increases speed and agility (A), and customers inherit AWS's physical and much of its network security under the shared responsibility model (E).

distractors.B: Security is a shared responsibility — the customer still secures data, IAM and configuration.
distractors.C: Customers never get control over physical infrastructure; AWS owns and operates it.
distractors.D: AWS does not operate customer applications, except under specific managed-service engagements.

explanation.concept: Decoupling contains the blast radius of a failure
explanation.correct: Decoupling reduces interdependencies between components — typically via queues or load balancers — so that when one component fails or slows, the others keep working.

distractors.A: Treating an application as one cohesive unit is the monolithic approach decoupling moves away from.
distractors.C: Decoupling breaks monoliths apart rather than making them easier to update as a whole.
distractors.D: Tracking API calls is AWS CloudTrail, unrelated to architectural coupling.

explanation.concept: Cost & Usage Report is the most granular record of what you were charged
explanation.correct: AWS Cost & Usage Reports contain the most detailed billing data available, broken down by service, resource and time period — the right tool for reviewing last month's EC2 charges.

distractors.A: AWS Budgets sets thresholds and alerts on future or ongoing spend; it is not a detailed historical report.
distractors.B: The Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a future architecture.
distractors.C: Systems Manager is for operational management of instances, not billing.

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing aggregates usage into higher volume-discount tiers
explanation.correct: Usage from all accounts is combined for pricing purposes, so the whole organization reaches volume-discount tiers sooner and every account benefits from the blended rate.

distractors.A: There is no flat 50% discount — savings come from tiering and RI sharing.
distractors.B: Consolidated billing produces genuine cost benefits, not merely organizational tidiness.
distractors.D: The AWS Free Tier applies once across the organization, not per member account.

explanation.concept: Protect EBS data with snapshots (durability) and encryption (confidentiality)
explanation.correct: Snapshots give you point-in-time backups stored durably in S3 (B), and encryption at rest protects the data if the underlying storage were ever accessed (C).

distractors.A: Firmware on the underlying hardware is AWS's responsibility; customers have no access to it.
distractors.D: Copying data to an external drive is neither practical nor part of the AWS model.
distractors.E: Physical data-centre access control is AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

explanation.concept: Elasticity provisions and releases resources as demand changes
explanation.correct: Elasticity means AWS resources are automatically provisioned when demand rises and released when it falls, so capacity tracks actual load instead of a fixed guess.

distractors.A: On-premises resources are physically fixed — you cannot scale them automatically.
distractors.B: A load balancer distributes traffic across existing targets; Auto Scaling changes how many exist.
distractors.C: Reducing interdependencies is decoupling, a different design principle.

explanation.concept: Two ways to alert on spend: CloudWatch billing alarms and AWS Budgets
explanation.correct: A CloudWatch billing alarm can publish to an SNS topic when estimated charges cross a threshold (A), and AWS Budgets can alert directly on a cost threshold (C). Both are legitimate answers.

distractors.B: Amazon SES sends email you compose yourself; it has no awareness of your bill.
distractors.D: CloudTrail logs API activity and cannot delete resources — and auto-deleting resources would be catastrophic anyway.
distractors.E: Amazon Connect is a contact-centre service, unrelated to billing.

explanation.concept: Edge locations are the CloudFront caching tier
explanation.correct: CloudFront caches content at edge locations — a far larger global network than Regions or AZs — so requests are served from a point physically close to the user.

distractors.A: Global Accelerator also uses the edge network but is a separate service for TCP/UDP traffic routing.
distractors.B: Regions are where your origin infrastructure runs, not the caching tier.
distractors.D: Availability Zones are data centre clusters within a Region, not caching points.

explanation.concept: Least privilege: the minimum permissions, for the minimum time
explanation.correct: Least privilege means granting only the permissions required to perform a task, only when required — and removing them when no longer needed.

distractors.B: Granting access to 'the core services' by default is broader than the task requires.
distractors.C: Blanket access for trusted users is the opposite of least privilege.
distractors.D: Granting no permissions at all would make users unable to work; the principle is minimum necessary, not zero.

explanation.concept: The three cloud service models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
explanation.correct: Networking as a Service is not one of the three standard cloud computing models. The recognised models are IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

distractors.A: PaaS is a standard model — you manage the application, the provider manages the platform.
distractors.B: IaaS is a standard model — you manage OS and above, the provider the hardware.
distractors.C: SaaS is a standard model — the provider manages everything, you just use the software.

explanation.concept: Match the storage class to the retrieval pattern
explanation.correct: The videos are almost never retrieved and only needed for rare legal or compliance events. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class in AWS, designed for exactly this long-term, rarely-accessed archive pattern.

distractors.A: Intelligent-Tiering suits unpredictable access patterns and costs more than Deep Archive for known-cold data.
distractors.B: AWS Marketplace is a software catalogue, not storage.
distractors.D: EBS is block storage attached to an EC2 instance — far more expensive and the wrong shape for archives.

explanation.concept: Route 53 is the DNS service (named after DNS port 53)
explanation.correct: Amazon Route 53 is the managed, highly available DNS web service, also handling domain registration and health-check-based routing policies.

distractors.B: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configuration changes for compliance.
distractors.C: CloudFront is the content delivery network.
distractors.D: Amazon EMR runs big-data frameworks such as Spark and Hadoop.
